Open the Asset Library tab in Location. 2. Select the Asset Library icon ![Asset Library.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438196351897) to open the default location for Button assets in the New Library Window. #### Add New Button Style & Apply 1. title: Rehost Software License Key to another environment
content: In order to move your software license key from one environment to another, please follow the steps below. * Please note that this rehost feature is only available if your software license key was generated as a “rehostable” type. ** If your Software License Key name includes “Rehostable” on the ACC page, you’re eligible to move a software license key to another environment. ([ACC Page](http://localhost:1947/_int_/devices.html)) **Step 1. Collect and Save Information - on a recipient device or PC** 1\. Open RUS on the destination machine that you want to transfer the SL license to ([**download**](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1vyPJ_ueKSbWWBUxKhZwM5K-hpmlHp4-l/view?usp=drive_link) the RUS) 2\. Click the ‘Transfer License’ tab on the top menu and click the box next to ‘Save recipient information to’. Then name the file according to your preference. 3\. Click ‘Collect and Save Information’, then the .id file will be saved on the destination machine. ![rus.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438428083865) **Step 2. Generate License Transfer File - on the original device or PC where the software license key is currently installed** 1\. Copy the .id file that was created from step 1 to the original machine which currently has the SL License installed. 2\. Open RUS and click the “Transfer License” tab. 3\. Find the software license key that you want to transfer under the ‘Key Type’ section and click. 4\. Load the .id file to ‘Read the recipient information file’ 5\. Click ‘Generate the license transfer file’ then name the file according to your preference. 6\. Click ‘Generate License Transfer File’ to create a .h2h file. ![rus1.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438428256665) ![rus2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438433915545) **Step 3. After generating the file, the license will disappear from the source machine. As a result, the software license key is no longer installed on the original environment.** ![rus3.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438434055193) **Step 4. Apply Update** 1\. Once the .h2h file is created, copy the .h2h file to the destination machine. 2\. Open RUS again and click ‘Apply License File’ to load the file. 3\. Click ‘Apply Update’ ![rus4.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438434200601) **Step 5. You can now check the transferred License on your destination machine on the ACC page****( Link to **[**ACC Page**](http://localhost:1947/_int_/devices.html)**)** ![rus5.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438434332569)
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for transferring a rehostable software license key between environments.

title: UV EDITOR MODE: UV Snapshot
content: ### Objective Saving UV as an image. (Ver. MD 7.5 +) ### Location Window ▶ UV Editor ▶ UV Snapshot Icon (Ver. 2025.0) Viewport Title Bar ▶ Right-click Dropdown menu ▶ UV Editor ▶ UV Snapshot Icon (2025.0) UV Editor mode Snapshot button on the toolbar at the top of the window. (up to Ver. 2024.2) ### Operation 1. Click the menu according to**Location.** 2. Click on the UV Snapshot icon. The Snapshot setting window will be opened. 3. Set the values for the following options below. Saving Path | Click the '...' folder icon button and set the saving directory and file format. Supports PNG and JPEG file formats. The background is not saved when saving PNG. When saving a JPEG, the background is saved as black. ---|--- Size (pixels) | Set the size of the image to be saved. The images are saved in a square with the same horizontal and vertical size. Antialiasing. If checked, anti-aliasing is applied to the wire segments. Anti-alias Lines (Ver. 2025.0) | When the Anti-alias Lines option is checked, anti-aliasing is applied to the wire segment. Wire Color | Sets the wire segment color. The color you set is not previewed in the UV correction window, and the corresponding color is applied when you save. UV Area | 0-1 (Default) | Save Default 0-1 Tile. A tile is a rectangular area between a single unit to a single unit. Selected Tile | Save a Selected Tile. If you enter the coordinates of U and V to be saved, one tile is saved accordingly. All Tiles | Save all Tile in which the UV appears 4. After setting values, click the save button to save the settings. The Snapshot image will be saved to the designated directory.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for saving UVs as images using the UV Snapshot feature in specific software versions.

title: Register Accessory: Hair/Shoes/Glasses/Earring/Hat .zacs (Ver. 2025.0)
content: ### Objective Register the Avatar's Hair/Shoes/Glasses/Earrings/Hat as an accessory file (ZACS). ### Location Main menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Register Accessory ### Operation #### **OBJ production** When making OBJ accessories in other 3D programs (Maya, 3ds Max, etc.), please follow the requirements below. * Set the work environment of the 3D program. (Axis: Y-Up, Unit: Millimeter) * Create a Hair/Shoes/Glasses/Earring/Hat OBJ according to the avatar file: Avatar | Prepare an avatar suitable for the Hair/Shoes to be registered. Marvelous Designer's default avatar or user avatar can be used. ---|--- Mesh | For the sharp angular expression, add an edge to the mesh to be reliably simulated in the Marvelous Designer. Dummy Mesh | For complex areas (shoelaces, heels, etc.) where the faces come into contact, wrap in a transparent and flat dummy mesh. Make the spacing between dummy meshes smaller and more consistent than shoe meshes. ![afceb30d-87c7-4216-9e12-09d416d724ce.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438327939353) Mesh Name | Hair | hair Shoes | ![5f603b9a-10ee-4566-99cc-a65d8cfc67e2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438282741017) (shoes_r, shoes_l) Glasses | (glasses_r, glasses_l) Earring | (earring_r, earring_l) Hat | hat Materials | Apply separately, various materials (leather, metal, plastic, etc.) Even if the heel is the same material, it must be applied separately, and the order must be at the bottom. ![9f3cb925-9f44-46fd-9c50-28b412f6a1ec.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438328277273)![25966d9e-df58-4556-9750-145229a14af1.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438328531481) * Set the transform properties. (Translate/ Rotation: All axes 0, Scale: All axes 1) ![512e752f-6fcf-4ab8-a1fa-2af6e68d2d83.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438333672089) * Export to FBX file. ※Note: * .obj files don't contain unit information internally * With autoscale enabled, software estimates units assuming human-sized objects * When using .obj files, remember and use the same unit setting during export and import * .fbx format stores unit information internally, making autoscale import work correctly ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438328861593) #### **Registering Accessories** 1. Open the avatar file for the Hair/Shoes/Glasses/Earrings/Hat to be registered to. ※ Note: It is recommended to review the placement of the (FBX) file (Hair/Shoes/Glasses/Earrings/Hat) that is intended to be registered and check that the position with the avatar is correct before you register it as an accessory. 2. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. → The Register Accessory window appears. 3. After setting the following options, click the Save button. Basic | Accessory Type | Hair | Select this option to register hair mesh. ---|---|---|--- Shoes | Select this option to register the shoe mesh. Glasses | Select this option to register glasses mesh. Earrings | Select this option to register the earring mesh. Hat | Select this option to register the hat mesh. Object | File | File | Select the mesh file path to register. Scale | Select the scale unit from Auto Scale/mm (Default) / cm (DAZ Studio) / in / ft / m / 8ft (Poster) / 8.6 ft (Poster). % | Set the scale of the mesh file. Axis Conversion | Set the axis direction for the cache data. The Y-axis runs vertically by default. Check the Invert box to invert the direction. Patterns | Select materials to register as accessories. Option | Thumbnail | Auto | A thumbnail will be generated automatically. Custom | Select this to add a custom thumbnail image. → The save file window appears. 4. Set the file name and path. → It is saved as a Hair/Shoes/Glasses/Earrings/Hat file (.ZACS). ※ Note: Make sure the mesh layer noted below has the correct nomenclature in Blender. The other names do not matter. Otherwise, you may encounter an error message that the name is wrong. #### **![mceclip0.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438329008153)**

title: ZIPPER: Zipper Slider and Stopper Properties
content: ### Objective Set and modify the Zipper Slider, puller and Stopper properties. ※ Note: The Puller, Slider, and Stopper of the zipper have been separated so that each can be individually selected and edited. (Ver. 2025.0). ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ### Operation * Select the tool indicated in Location. * Select a Zipper or Stopper created on a 3D Garment and modify its properties: Option | Description ---|--- Name | Customize the name of the zipper. Type (Ver. 2025.0) | One Way | One slider and puller is shown. Two Way | Two sliders and pullers are shown which can be moved in opposite directions. Direction (Ver. 2025.0) | Direction can be configured when the type is set to Two Way. Bottom to Bottom | Slider and Puller will be positioned near the Stopper, at the end of the zipper. Head to Head | Slider and Puller will be positioned of the original position. Shape | Slider | Select a shape for the slider. Puller | Select a shape for the puller. Stopper | Select the Stopper type (Open / Closed End) and then select shapes for Top and Bottom. (ver MD10) ※ Note: A selection of Bottom shapes is configured based on the shape of the Stopper. Specification | Gauge | Select the size of the Slider by Gauge or percentage. Weight (g) | Assign the weight of the slider. (Ver 4.2) Fasten Zipper | Reverse Zip Direction | Select the zip direction. The slider is relocated based on the option. Move to Opposite Side | Select a side of the zipper tape where the slider will locate when the zipper is open. Material | Configure the Slider's Type, Texture, Color, and Opacity. ※ Note: Uncheck Use Same Material as Slider after selecting the Puller or Stopper tab to assign material separately. (Ver. 10) Polygon Optimization (Ver. 2024.0) | Count | Set the number of polygons. Plane | This is applied in the form of a texture when the Plane is activated. Count cannot be set on Plane activation. ※ Note: * Adjust the weight of the Slider
content_description: This web page provides users with detailed instructions on how to set and customize the properties of Zipper Sliders, Pullers, and Stoppers within a 3D garment design tool.

Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu▶ File ▶ Snapshot ▶ 3D Window (F10) → Save File pop-up window appears. 2\. Each image has a drop down menu to change orientation. The number of images are set by the number in Layout Refresh the images with refresh button Open existing Multi-view file (.mvs) Save custom multi-view (.mvs) options for future use ---|---|--- Images in preview | Select camera orientation from the following options: * Front * 3/4 Left * Right * Left * Back * 3/4 Right * Top * Bottom * Custom ※Note: To create a custom view based on current camera view: Hover your Mouse-over on the preview image ▶ Click on the camera icon in the left hand corner. Custom | Customize view angle in 3D window. Mouse-over on the preview image ▶ Click on the camera icon Single Image Size | Preset | Customize or select from provided preset options. title: Avatar: Register Pose/Motion
content: ### Objective Register the motion from FBX file as the motion files compatible with Marvelous Designer Template avatars. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Register Pose/Motion ### ### Operation 1. Click the Main Menu » Avatar » **Register Pose/Motion**. → A popup window with message "All avatars and garments in 3D Window will be deleted. Do you want to proceed?" Click **Proceed** Button if you want to continue. 2. In the Register Pose/Motion window, select the type to register, either **Pose** or **Motion**. 3. Open the FBX file by clicking on the **folder![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438377062425)** button. 4. Select the Gender of the compatible CLO avatar and select the Shoe Type for female. 5. For motion, switch to Animation mode to play loaded motion as needed. 6. Click the **Save** button to save as the Pose(*.pos) or Motion(*.mtn) file. ### Register Pose/Motion window Type | Pose | Register and save as pose (*.pos) file type. ---|---|--- Motion | Register and save as motion (*.mtn) file type. File (FBX) | Select the FBX file with animation to use for registering. Option Gender | Female | Register the pose / Motion to female template avatar. Shoe Type | Select between **Heels** and **flat** shoe types. This setting will affect heel joint rotation of the character. Male | Register the pose / Motion to male template avatar. Kid | Register the pose / Motion to kid template avatar. Region (for motion *.mtn file type only) | Entire | Register the animation from the FBX file to entire region. Play Only | Register the animation from the FBX file to set play region only. Current Frame | Register the animation from the FBX file to current frame. ###
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to guide users through the process of registering poses and motions from FBX files for compatibility with Marvelous Designer's template avatars.

title: Fabric Style Window
content: ### Objective Add and organize fabric style and apply it to the garment. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Fabric Style Tab (ver. 2025.0) Main Menu ▶ Window ▶ Object Browser ▶ Fabric Style Tab (ver. 2025.0) ### ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438423459353) Operation #### Open Fabric Asset Library 1. Open the Fabric Library tab in Location. 2. Select the Asset Library icon ![Asset Library.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438423651097) to open the default location for Fabric Style assets in the New Library Window. #### Add Fabric Style & Apply 1. Select the tool/menu indicated. 2. Click +Add at the top right. Or add a Fabric file by dragging it to the Fabric tab or on the 3D garment. → A Fabric style is added. Click Copy at the top right. → A Fabric style is duplicated. 3. Drag the style to the 3D/2D pattern and apply it. Or after selecting a pattern first, click the Assign button to the right of the Fabric tab or Fabric style. → The Fabric is applied to the pattern. 4. By clicking the left square icon located on the right of the Fabric name, you can toggle texture mapping type between Unified Map / Texture Repeat. Unified Map: Displays textures based on the pattern layout in the UV map. Texture Repeat: Repeatedly displays the texture across the pattern. 5. Click the Plus icon located on the left of the bin icon, to add prints to your Fabric. Select your print image and open. You can still change the Unified Map / Texture Repeat by clicking the icon from process #4. Adjust the Material Property Editor. #### Group Setting (ver. 2025.0) 1. To set Fabric Groups, Click the Create New Folder button at the top left of the Fabric tab. → A new folder group is created. 2. Click the Add Fabric or Open Fabric Files buttons on the right side of the group to load the Fabric file. → A Fabric style is added or opened to the group. 3. Click the Edit Folder Name button on the left of the group to edit the name. 4. Click and Drag the Fabric to different groups. → Right click on the Fabric, select Drop as Copying, to drop the fabric to the other group folder to copy. This allows to keep the Fabric in the original group folder while making a copied Fabric in the new group folder. → Right click on the Fabric, select Drop as Moving, to drop the fabric to the other group folder.
content_description: This webpage serves as a comprehensive guide for adding, organizing, and applying fabric styles to garments within the Fabric Style Tab of the Object Browser in version 2025.0.

title: Create Smooth Curve
content: ### ### ### ### ### Objective Modify Pattern outlines or Internal Lines into smooth curves. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Smooth Curve 2D Toolbar ▶ Smooth Curve ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Smooth Curve 2D Toolbar ▶ Smooth Curve 2. Click on a segment or point to establish the first point. → The point appears in grey. 3. Drag the mouse. → A grey arrow extending from the point follows the cursor. 4. Click on another segment or point to establish the endpoint. → A reference line is created between the two points. 5. With the reference line created, click on the side that will be converted into a smooth curve. → The entire side is highlighted in yellow. 6. Click & drag the reference line to create the desired smooth curve. → The entire outline of the selected side is replaced by the reference line. ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438534208793) ### Updated in 2025.0 Curvature of a specific line can be precisely adjusted without affecting other lines. 1. Click a start point and endpoint on the segment or point to set the editing range. 2. Select which side to be edited. 3. Click and drag a segment or point to adjust curvature within the set range. * **Edit** * By default, nearby points adjust proportionally when moving. * You can move only the selected point by holding the [ D ] key while dragging. * Right-click while dragging the segment or point to enter a specific moving distance. * **Add** * Click a segment while holding the [ Ctrl ] key to add a curve point. _* Adding to a Bezier curve points convert it to free curve points, which may adjust the curvature._ * **Delete** * Right-click a point and click the Delete menu to delete selected points. 4. Press Enter to complete. * When selecting a pattern outline or internal line, update based on the edited pattern outline or internal line. * When selecting a reference line, update based on the edited reference line. Segment points will be added at the start and end. * ※ Note: #### Cancel Actions * Cancel All Actions: While using the Smooth Curve tool, press Esc or Ctrl + Z on the keyboard and all actions are undone. * Cancel Last Action: While using the Smooth Curve tool, press Delete or Backspace on the keyboard and the last action is undone.
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for using the Smooth Curve tool to transform pattern outlines or internal lines into smooth curves in a 2D design environment.

title: Project File (*.ZPrj) Open/Save
content: ### Objective Compress the various files used for Garment creation into one file, and save it. ※ Note: #### Files included in Project (*.zprj) files * *.avt file, with all Avatar-related data [Avatar, Accessories, Arrangement Bounding Volumes, Arrangement Points, Avatar Size, Poses] * If there are multiple Avatars, they are all saved within the Project file (ver2.3.0). * *.zpac file, containing all Garment-related data (3D Garments, 2D Patterns, Fabrics, subsidiary Materials) * *.anm file, if an Animation has been recorded * Any 3D environment settings (Wind, Light, Ground, Background Image/Color, Scenes/Props) * Simulation options set by the user (ver2.3.0). ### Location #### Open Project File Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open ▶ Project (Ctrl+O) #### Save/Save Over Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save Project (Ctrl+S) #### Save As Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶ Project (Ctrl+Shift+S) #### New Project (ver. 12.1) Main Menu ▶ File ▶ New Project (Ctrl+N) ### Operation #### Open Project File 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open ▶ Project (Ctrl+O) → The Open File window opens. 2. Select the desired file and click OK to load the file. ※ Note: Double-click the Project file *.zprj or drag and drop it onto the 3D window to open it. 3. Apply any detailed settings, then click on the OK button Load Type | Open a new project file or Add the file additionally. If you add additional files, you can set the position of the object in the X, Y, and Z Axis. ---|--- Object | Enables the selective import of object types included in the project file. * Garment * Avatar * 3D State * Custom View * Scene and Props * Display Settings #### Save Over Project File 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save Project (Ctrl+S) → The original Project file is overwritten. #### Save Project File 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶ Project (Ctrl+Shift+S) → The Open File window opens. 2. Select a location to save the Garment file. 3. Enter the Project name into the File Name tab and press Save to save the file. → A Project file *.zprj will be created along with its thumbnail image. #### New Project (ver. 12.1) 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ New Project (Ctrl+N) → The existing file will be closed and a new “Untitled” project file will be created.
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for users to efficiently compress and save all essential files related to garment creation into a single project file.

title: TOPSTITCH PROPERTIES: Topstitch Corner Type
content: ### Objective Set Topstitch corner type to extend the stitch more smoothly at corners. ※ Note: If stitch type is Overlock, set the corner type to Curved for smoother extension. ### Location 2D Pattern Window ▶ Edit Topstitch ▶ Topstitch Property Editor ▶ Corner ### Operation #### Curved Corner 1. Select a Topstitch with the Edit Topstitch tool in the 2D window to change its properties. → Topstitch properties appear on the Property Editor. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Topstitch Property Editor ▶ Curved ▶ On → The selected Topstitch is now curved and smoothly extended. #### Right Angled Corner 1. Select a Topstitch with the Edit Topstitch tool in the 2D window to change its properties. → Topstitch properties appear on the Property Editor. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Topstitch Property Editor ▶ Right Angled ▶ On → The selected topstitch is now being curved at a right angle. #### Topstitching Smooth Corner 1. Select a Topstitch with the Edit Topstitch tool in the 2D window to change its properties. → Topstitch properties appear on the Property Editor. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Topstitch Property Editor ▶ Smooth ▶ On → The selected Topstitch is now curved and smoothly extended. Set this to continue naturally if the edge of the Topstitch is broken.
content_description: This webpage provides instructions for adjusting the corner type of topstitch properties to achieve smoother transitions at corners in your 2D pattern designs.

title: Seamline Property (ver. 2025.0)
content: ### Objective Adjust Seamline properties such as line types, tension, sublayers, topstitch, puckering, and 3D Seamline Normal Maps to render a realistic Garment. ### ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Edit Sewing (B) 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Sewing (B) ### Operation 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Click on any point or segment of the Sewing Line to display the Property Editor. Properties | Description ---|--- Seam | Open | Open a Sewing Style Preset File (*.ssp). Save | The current properties can be saved as a Sewing Style Preset File (.ssp) type file. Information | Name | Set the name of the currently selected sewing line. Sewing Line Type | Turned (Off) | Fold Strength | The intensity of the fold is able to be set by adjusting the value of Fold Strength. The higher the value, the closer the fold is to the set angle. When a jacket and its lining are sewn together, the sewn area inflates due to the default sewing angle and intensity values. In this case, set the Fold Strength to 0 to flatten the sewn boundaries. Fold Angle | 180° represents a flat state. The internal line is folded towards the front of the pattern as the fold angle is closer to 0˚ and is folded into the back of the pattern as the angle is closer to 360˚. Turned (On) | Sew two layers of pattern flatly. The Fold Strength and Fold Angle settings cannot be adjusted. ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438049347737) Tension | When the 3D garment is expressed as being stretched more than the actual garment, adjust the Tension of Sewing Line. Same as the actual real life concept, Tension is applied based on the short or long side with the Ease and Stretch options. Sewing Line Type | Ease | When the seam lengths differ, this type adds a slight allowance, resulting in a relatively soft sewing tension. Stretch | When the seam lengths differ, this type does not add any allowance, resulting in a more precise and higher sewing tension. Strength | Increase or decrease the strength of the sewing tension by entering the value. The result may vary depending on the Strength even with the same Ratio value. Ratio | Adjust the sewing tension's ratio to express varying drape effects by different sewing methods. Set Sublayer | Assign orders to the Sewing Lines on a Pattern that folds on itself such as seam allowances and pleats, to increase simulation stability. Reverse Direction | Swap the order of the Sewing Line and the Sewed Line. Sublayer | Decide which side of the fabric is attached to the fixed Sewing Line, Back or Front. Topstitch | Name | Rename the Topstitch. Topstitch Property | Change the style of the selected Topstitch. Extend | When the start or end point of a Topstitch does not reach or sticks out of the Pattern outline, extend it to fit to the Pattern. Corner | Curved | Set the Topstitch corner type to extend the stitch more smoothly at corners. Right Angled | Set the Topstitch to be a right angle in the corner of the pattern. Smooth | Set it to continue naturally if the edge of the Topstitch is broken. Offset | Set the Z Offset of the Topstitch. Placement | Seam A | Topstitch will be shown only on Seam A. Seam B | Topstitch will be shown only on Seam B. Seam Both | Topstitch will be shown on both sides. Puckering | Name | Rename the Puckering. Puckering Property | Change the style of the selected Topstitch. Extend | Extend the start/endpoint of the puckering to the 2D pattern outline. Offset | Offset (mm) | Adjust the distance between the puckering and the pattern outline. Include the Puckering Width in Offset or not if needed. Z Offset (mm) | Adjust the distance between the Z-axis and a pattern piece. Placement | Seam A | Puckering will be shown only on Seam A. Seam B | Puckering will be shown only on Seam B. Seam Both | Puckering will be shown on both sides. 3D Seamline | Plain Seam | Normal Map | Select an image to be used as the Normal Map. Intensity | Adjust the intensity of the Normal Map applied to the seamline. Thickness (mm) | Adjust the thickness of the Normal Map applied to the seamline. Directional | Placement | Select Seam A or Seam B for the placement of the seamline. Normal Map | Select an image to be used as the Normal Map. Intensity | Adjust the intensity of the Normal Map applied to the seamline. Thickness (mm) | Adjust the thickness of the Normal Map applied to the seamline.
content_description: This web page provides comprehensive tools and settings for adjusting seamline properties to enhance the realism of garment simulations in 3D design.

title: ZIPPER: Zipper Tape Properties
content: ### Objective Modify the Zipper tape properties. ### ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Zipper Tape (Click On Zipper Tape)▶ Property Editor ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Zipper Tape (Click On Zipper Tape)▶ Property Editor → The properties of the selected Zipper Tape appear in the Property Editor. 2. Modify the Zipper Tape properties based on the available options below: **Properties** | **Description** ---|--- Name | Rename the Zipper Tape. Line Length | Edit the length of the Zipper teeth. Preset (ver. 2025.0) | Set the preset of the Zipper from Custom, Plastic_01, Plastic_02, Metal, Nylon, Reverse_Nylon, Invisible. Texture (ver. 2025.0) | Set the Teeth type to Texture or OBJ. Size (ver.11) | Set the size of the Zipper. Teeth Width | Enter directly the width of the Zipper to adjust. Total Width | Adjust the Tape width of the Zipper. Width | Set the width of the Zipper Tape. The texture image changes based on the width entered. Thickness | Set the Zipper Tape Thickness. Particle Distance | Adjust zipper tape's Particle Distance. Fasten Zipper | Zip or unzip the Zipper. Fold | Adjust the Strength of the fold for Sewing between the Zipper and Pattern. Material | Set the Material Type, Texture, Color and Opacity of the Zipper Teeth and Tape. Physical Property | Adjust physical properties to the selected zipper teeth.
content_description: This web page serves as a guide for modifying the properties of Zipper Tape within a 3D design environment, detailing the steps and options available in the Property Editor.

title: Custom UI Layout (ver. 2025.0)
content: ### Objective Make a custom user-defined UI layout: including the state of open windows, docking positions, and window sizes, can be saved and reloaded as needed, allowing for efficient optimization of the workspace. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Window ▶ Layout ### Operation 1. Dock individual windows to your preferred positions and adjust their width and height as desired. 2. Click **Export Layout** in the Layout menu, enter a name for custom UI layout in the dialog that appears, then click **OK**. 3. The UI Layout will be saved under the **Custom Layouts** group in the Layout Menu, and a *.uix file will be saved in the default directory. 4. Click **Browse Directory** to open the folder where the file has been saved. 5. Clicking on any item under either **Layouts (System Default)** or **Custom Layouts** will load the corresponding saved layout. ※ Note: The Layout list is synchronized with the default folder. You can back up any desired layout files separately and paste them into this folder to reuse them after reinstalling the software.
content_description: Create and manage custom user-defined UI layouts to optimize your workspace by saving and reloading your preferred window arrangements effortlessly.

title: Compatible File Format
content: ### File | Format | Import | Export | Detail ---|---|---|---|--- 3D | FBX | *.fbx | O | O | File contains Mesh, Material, Joint, Animation, and Camera information. *Only Joint that was imported as FBX to Marvelous Designer can be exported as FBX. OBJ | *.obj | O | O | File contains Geometry and Material Information. Primarily used for importing Avatar and related sources into the program. Alembic | *.abc | O | O | Is an interchange file format for computer graphics that saves both vertex and animation information. ※ Mac export (ver. 5.1.431) Open COLLADA | *.dae | O | X | This file can be exported from other 3D softwares such as 3ds Max, Maya and used. These files contain geometry and material, in addition to rigging, skinning, and animation data When exporting OpenCOLLADA files from 3DS Max or Maya, install the “OpenCOLLADA plugin ([http://www.opencollada.org](http://www.opencollada.org/)) and export to use the avatar USD | *.usd | O | O | File contains Mesh, Material, Joint, Animation, Camera, and Scene Layout information. Serves as a universal interchange format for 3D content across various applications and platforms. For more information, please see the [USD file compatibility page.](USD%20file%20Compatibility) USDZ (ver. 2025.0) | *.usdz | X | O | File contains Mesh, Material, Joint, Animation, Camera, and Scene Layout information. It is a compressed package format that combines all 3D assets into a single file. Primarily used for AR/VR applications and interactive 3D content. Animation Cache | *.mc *.pc2 *.mdd | O | O | Is the vertex animation data. It is possible to take animations made in Marvelous Designer to 3DSMax or Maya in point cache format. LXO | *.lxo | X | O | File contains Geometry and Material Information. Used to export Apparel/Avatar information to Modo in the LXO file format. 3D Snapshot | *.png | - | O | Ability to save single views of the 3D window in the PNG file format. 2D | Texture | *.jpg, *.png, etc. | O | O | Textures inserted into garments, use image textures in formats such as JPG, PNG, TIF, and PSD. Supported file types: jpg, jpeg, png, bmp, wbmp, psd, ico, tga, tif, tiff, gif, mng, jng, dds, hdr, koa, lbm, iff, pbm, pcd, pcx, pgm, ppm, ras, cut, xmb, xpm, sgi, g3, exr, j2k, jp2, pfm, pict, pct) Substance | *.sbsar | O | - | File contains procedural texture information with adjustable parameters. The separate channels of a Substance material can be baked and exported (color, normal, metalness, roughness, opacity)
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide to the various file formats supported for import and export in 3D design software, detailing their specific contents and applications.

title: Scene Browser (2025.0)
content: ### Objective Quickly view and navigate between existing assets in the 3D scene. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Scene Tab Main Menu ▶ Window ▶ Object Browser ▶ Scene Tab Right-click "Browser" Title Bar ▶ Object Browser ▶ Scene Tab ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438121644697) ### Operation Double click and expand the groups to easily change names and quickly get to the specific property editor where applicable. 2D Pattern | Expand to view all pattern assets in the scene. Double clicking asset's name to change the name (Also found in the Pattern Property Editor ▶ Information ▶ Name) ---|--- Sewing | Expand to view all sewing relationships in the scene. Double clicking asset's name to change the name (Also found with Edit Sewing tool ▶ Sewing Relationship/ Seam ▶ Property Editor ▶ Name) 3D Form | Lists the Hierarchy of each imported asset including the Joints and mesh assets. Double-click on each of the names to change them, or change the name in the Property Editor. Material | Any Style Groups (aside from Fabric) Graphic, Buttons, Buttonholes, Topstitching, Puckering and Trims will populate here. Double-click the asset name to change the name and open the Camera Property Editor Light | Lists the Hierarchy of each imported Light asset. title: Topstitch Style Window (ver. 2025)
content: ### Objective Add and organize Topstitch styles and apply it to the Topstitching in the scene. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Topstitching Style Tab (ver. 2025.0) Main Menu ▶ Window ▶ Object Browser ▶ Topstitching Style Tab (ver. 2025.0) ### ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438180990489) Operation #### Open Asset Library 1. title: Simulation Properties
content: ### Objective Configure the simulation properties for advanced scene settings. ### Location Object Browser ▶ ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358131961369) Scene ▶ Environment ▶ Simulation Properties Right-Click 3D background ▶ 3D Background Options ▶ Simulation Properties ### Operation 1. Select the tool/menu indicated. → The simulation properties appear in the Property Editor. 2. Refer to the below table and edit the simulation properties as needed. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- Use the Folder Icon to open the File Explorer to import a custom setting. Use the Save icon to save custom settings. Preset | Instead of selecting the [simulation mode](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358232630937) from the 3D toolbar, you can choose predefined presets below are primarily used. * Normal (Default) * Animation (Stable) * Fitting (accurate Fabric) Time Step | This determines the time values calculated within the simulation engine. The smaller you set it, the more sophisticated it will be, but it will also require more calculations and will, resultingly, be slower. The default values are recommended. Simulations Per Frame (Simulation Quality) | When calculating cloth simulation for a given time step, this denotes how many substeps one simulation calculation is divided into. For example, if you are calculating a time step of 0.03 and number of simulation is 10, the actual time step will be 0.003. Simulating multiple times with these smaller time intervals ensures both more numerically accurate results and stable collision handling, but takes much longer. CG Finish Condition | Clothing simulation is the process of solving a large linear system. Large linear systems can be solved using a numerical analysis method called conjugate gradient method (CG). CG improves the accuracy of the answer through iterative calculations. The condition for CG ending can be set by the number of iterations or when the error (=residual) falls below a certain value. CG Iteration Count | Iteration: Because it repeats only a certain number of times and ends unconditionally, it is faster but may be less accurate. CG Residual | Residual: It is slower but can be more accurate because it stops when the error falls below a certain value. Self Collision Iteration Count | Defines the number of collision calculations for the clothing. More collision calculations produce more precise results, but they are also slower. Please use the default value. Air Damping | The resistance that the garment receives from the air. Gravity | Defines the most important gravity values in your simulation. If this value is adjusted, simulation results will become unrealistic. Please use the default value, unless you want to, for example, create a weightless simulation. Default is -9800 (0 results in no gravity and positive values can achieve other interesting results) Number of CPU in Use | This determines the number of physical cores within the CPU that will be used for the simulation. Marvelous Designer can technically use up to 12 cores, which are automatically defined based on your computer. Even if it is a high-end CPU with 16 cores, up to 12 can be used. This may vary depending on the CPU manufacturer and actual CPU products. This value is best also left at default. Nonlinear Simulation | Linear or non-linear is an important factor in all fields of computer graphics, simulation, rendering and engineering. By analogy, the real world is non-linear, but computer implementations are linear. Nonlinearity is a technique that makes things look very real, and simulating them this way is sophisticated, but slow. If Fitting simulation is run, this option is selected. t's slower because it's more complicated and requires a lot of calculations. **Collision Simulation Options** Ground | All of these are intended to simulate collisions and friction between the clothing and the avatar. Because Marvelous Designer calculates numerous contacts and collisions between the fabric and the body, the simulation looks natural and realistic. It is recommended that these values are also left at their default. ---|--- Avatar-Cloth Collision Detection | Toggle On/ Off * Triangle-vertex * Edge-Edge Self-Collision Detection | Toggle On/ Off * Triangle-vertex * Edge-Edge Avoidance Stiffness (adjustable property, default is [0.001000] ) Proximity Detection | Toggle On/ Off * Triangle-vertex * Edge-Edge **Collision Resolution Options** Intersection Resolution | Toggle on / off Allow Normal / Flipped Normal values to set direction and resolve intersecting mesh issues. ---|--- Layer Based Collision Detection | Toggle on / off Allow layers & Sublayers to set Collision values. (example: layer 1 will be on top of layers 0 and below) ※ Note: Use the Open &Save buttons on the top of the Property Editor to save, open, and reuse the settings.
content_description: This web page provides essential guidance for configuring simulation properties to achieve advanced scene settings in Marvelous Designer.

title: Avatar IK Joint Mapping (2025.0)
content: ### Objective Streamline IK joint mapping for various avatars to achieve natural movement while ensuring seamless compatibility for motions and poses across all avatars. The avatar must have properly defined joint points. Rigging must include key joints such as shoulders, elbows, wrists, pelvis, knees, and ankles. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ IK Joint tab ### IK Joint Mapping ※ Note: The FBX file must not contain joints with duplicate names, and IK mapping may not apply correctly for creatures or quadruped avatars with non-human structures. Joints are categorized into required and optional, and you must map all required joints to ensure proper IK setup. ![IK.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438084949529) For optional joints, we recommend mapping those indicated in the image if they are present in the avatar to achieve more accurate results. ## ![IK_Optional.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438039415193) **1\. Auto Mapping** If the avatar meets the following conditions, click the Auto Mapping at the top right to apply automatic mapping. • If each joint name of the avatar matches that of the Marvelous Designer avatar. • If the avatar is from one of the following platforms: Daz 3D, Adobe Mixamo, Reallusion Character Creator, or Unreal Engine MetaHuman. **2\. Manual Mapping** 1\. Click the desired item from the image or list in the IK Mapping tab, then click the joint to be mapped on the avatar in the 3D Window. * Alternatively, you can first click the joint on the avatar and then click an item from the tab. 2\. When Symmetry Mapping option at the top right is turned on, the corresponding joint on the opposite side is automatically mapped. Note that both sides must be named as follows: Left_/Right_, L_ / R_,Left / Right,_L / _R,_Left / _Right. 3\. Once all mapping is set up, adjust IK Pose. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438053745049) ### Set Pose Set the avatar in a T-pose to ensure proper compatibility with Marvelous Designer avatar pose and motion files apply correctly. 1\. Adjust the avatar’s joints directly to a T-pose using the gizmo in the 3D window. * If the avatar is already in a T-pose, this step can be skipped. 2\. Click the Set T-Pose at the top right. **※ Note:** • If set correctly, the Reset Pose activates, allowing you to check the set T-pose when clicked. • After adjusting the pose during IK mapping, click the Reset Pose button to revert the avatar to the set T-pose. **Open/Save** You can manage the IK data mapped to the avatar as a file. * Click Open/Save at the top right to open or save IK data as a .iks file. * IK files are only compatible between avatars that have been mapped.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to guide users through the process of streamlining IK joint mapping for various avatars to ensure natural movement and seamless compatibility across motions and poses.

Show | Select or deselect Weft / Warp / Shear to be included in the fit properties. Pressure | Range Color Count | Select 8 or 4 for the range count. Range | kPa | Displays the force per unit area in kPa applied to a garment by external stress. Represents the internal stress and tension in the fabric itself when stretched. gf/cm2 | Displays the force per unit area in gf/cm2 applied to a garment by external stress. Measures the actual pressure exerted by the garment on the body surface. mmHg | Displays the force per unit area in mmHg applied to a garment by external stress. title: [Beta] Fur Rendering in 3D Window (ver. 2025.0)
content: ### Objective Express fur more realistically by adjusting Fur Parameters and Fur Shape to visualize different shaped and color fur in the 3D window. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Fabric ▶ Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Type ▶ Fur_Strand ### Operation 1. Apply the Fur_Strand material from the material type option, referring to the **'Location'** indicated above. * Fur can be previewed in 3D Window with Default Render and Quality Render, and Interactive Render. 2. Select one of the presets to express Fox, Mink, Angora, Sherpa and more. **Fur Material Properties** **Properties** | **Description****** ---|--- Texture Mapping | Repeat | Controls how many times the texture pattern repeats across the fur surface. Higher values create more repetitions of the pattern, resulting in a denser appearance. Unified | When enabled, applies the texture consistently across all fur strands for a uniform look. When disabled, each strand uses the texture based on its individual position, creating more natural variation. Type | Select Fur_Strand to edit Fur Parameters and Fur Shape. Fur Preset | Select Fur preset from Default, Angora, Fox, Mink Skin, Mohair, Muskrat Belly, Plush, Rabbit, Raw Edge Denim, Terry Cloth and Custom. Materials | Set the [Fabric properties](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358364198425). Fur Parameters | Melanin | Configure the saturation of the fur's original color. Higher Melanin values create more saturated colors, while lower values result in lighter colors. Pheomelanin | Configure how reddish the fur appears. Higher Pheomelanin values create redder fur. The Pheomelanin value is applied proportionally to the Melanin value and has no effect when Melanin is set to 0. Glossiness | Configure the shininess of the fur. Higher values make the fur appear shinier when light is applied. Softness | Adjust the smoothness of the fur. Higher Softness values create smoother fur, while lower values result in rougher fur. Fur Gradation Color | Color | Select the mid and the tip color of the gradation. Position | Adjust the length of the fur where Mid and Tip Color is applied. Interpolation | Naturally blend the borders of tip, mid, and root colors. Fur Shape | Base | Length (mm) | Configure the length of the fur. Higher the value is, longer the fur is. Thickness (mm) | Configure the thickness of a single thread of the fur. Higher the value is, thicker the fur is. Bend | Configure the bending strength of the fur. Higher the value is, more affected by the gravity and bends more. Taper | Differentiate the thickness of the fur between its root and the end. Higher the value is, thinner the fur becomes toward the end. On the other hand, lower the value is, similar the thickness is between the root and the end. Density (inch2) | Configure how fur are closely placed. Higher the value is, more dense the fur is. On the other hand, lower the value is, more scattered the fur is. Segments | Configure how many sections a single thread of fur is divided into. When the fur is long and has higher Bending value, the fur must have higher Segments value to express the Bending smoothly and realistically. However, for the short and straight fur, the Segments value is not as significant. Maps | Use Base Maps to express different length, thickness, density, curl, gravity, bend, bend direction and initial direction within a single Pattern. 0 is multiplied to the values when a Map is black. On the other hand, 1 is multiplied to the values when a Map is white. ![renderoutput.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438303075481) Gravity | Force | Apply the force of gravity. Vector | Manually apply the Gravity value to each axis. Curl | Radius (mm) | Configure the size of the curl. Higher values create larger curls, while lower values create smaller curls. Number | Configure the number of curls. Higher values create more curls in the fur, while lower values create fewer curls. Variance | Length | Express uniform or irregular fur length. Higher values create more irregular fur lengths, while lower values create more uniform lengths. Thickness | Express uniform or irregular fur thickness. Higher values create more irregular fur thickness, while lower values create more uniform thickness. Direction | Express uniform or irregular fur bending direction. Higher values create more irregular bending directions, while lower values create more uniform bending directions. Gravity | Express uniform or irregular gravity effect. Higher values create more irregular gravity effects, while lower values create more uniform gravity effects. ※Note: Gravity effect only applies when the Bending value is not 0. Curl Radius | Express uniform or irregular curl radius. Higher values create more irregular curl radius, while lower values create more uniform curl radius. Randomization | Seed | Change the seed value to generate a different random pattern for the fur. Each seed creates a unique but consistent variation. 3. Select a fur preset from Physical Properties and fine-tune the physical property details to meet your specific requirements. ※Note: * Fur Strand is supported only in the window system at this moment. * Fur Strand is not currently supported for macOS due to rendering speed considerations. * Fur_Strand can be applied to all objects except Avatar and Stitch. * If you create Fur_Strand and export USD, there would be an option to include fur strand data.
content_description: "Explore and customize realistic fur textures and shapes in a 3D environment by adjusting various fur parameters and presets."

content: UV Selection Arraying individual UV Arraying all UV UV Packing * * * ## ## UV Selection UVs can be selected in several ways as described below. **Select All with Same Property** and **Select All Sewn Patterns** can be executed from the right-click pop-up menu of the selected UV. **Single Selection** | Click to select the desired UV. Hold Shift and click to add UVs to the previous selection. Multiple UVs can be selected by dragging. ---|--- **Select All with Same Property** | **Particle Distance** | Selects all Patterns that have the same particle distance. **Layer** | Selects all Patterns that have the same layer value. **Fabric** | Selects all Patterns with the same applied fabric. **Select All Sewn Patterns** | Selects all Patterns that have a direct or indirect sewing relationship with the selected Pattern. * * * ## Arraying individual UV ### Objective Arraying selected individual UV. ### Location Window ▶ UV editor mode ▶ UV right-click popup menu Viewport Title Bar ▶ Right-click Dropdown menu ▶ UV Editor ▶ UV right-click popup menu (ver. 2025.0) ### Operation Align | Left, Center, Right, Top, Middle, Bottom | Selected UVs will be aligned by a selected standard.
